english.title: Employer fail to discharge general health, safety and welfare duty to employee

additionalkeywords.additionalkeyword: Health and Safety at work Act 1974

english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being an employer, failed to ensure, so far as was reasonably practicable, the health, safety and welfare at work of all your employees in that **(..SPECIFY FAILURE..)
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 2 and 33(1)(a) of, and Schedule3A to, the Health and Safety at Work etc Act 1974.
english.pointstoprove:

english.notes:
(i) See section 2(2) of the Act for examples of the extent of the employer's duty.
(ii) Proceedings for an offence shall not, in England and Wales, be instituted except by an inspector or the Environment Agency or by or with the consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions, see section 38 of the Health and Safety at Work etc Act 1974.

other.penalty:
Either way -
Summary: 6/12 months imprisonment and / or a fine.
Indictment: 2 years imprisonment and / or a fine.

The maximum penalty on summary conviction is 6 months for offences committed before 2nd May 2002; for offences committed on or after that date it may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see Schedule 3A to the Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974 and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2020.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
